headline: Rupee Closes Above 93 for First Time in Seven Months, at 92.67 to the Dollar
subheadline: A fifth straight session of gains, powered by ₹84,290 crore of foreign equity inflows in nine November sessions and weaker crude, took the rupee past a level it last closed above on April 10.
body:
• The rupee settled 65 paise higher at 92.67 (provisional) against the US dollar on Friday, November 20, closing above the 93 level for the first time in over seven months.
  • It was the fifth consecutive session of gains; the currency has appreciated over 1.6 per cent since its November 13 close of 94.19.
  • Foreign investors pumped in Rs 84,290 crore into Indian equities over nine trading sessions from November 2 to 13, after net withdrawals in September and October.
  • For readers sending money to India, $1,000 now converts to about Rs 92,670 before fees and provider margins, compared with about Rs 94,190 at the November 13 close.

The Indian rupee closed above the 93-per-dollar level on Friday for the first time in more than seven months, settling 65 paise higher at 92.67 (provisional) against the US dollar, according to PTI. The fifth consecutive session of gains followed uninterrupted inflows of foreign funds and a rally in domestic stocks.

At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 93.25 and touched an intraday high of 92.65, climbing above the 93 level for the first time since April 10, when it closed at 92.83 against the dollar. On Thursday it had settled 9 paise higher at 93.32. Hindu BusinessLine's intraday report put the currency at 92.82 earlier in the session as it crossed the mark.

Foreign money is doing the heavy lifting

Forex analysts attributed the rupee's strength to foreign institutional investors chasing higher returns amid a weaker American currency and waning AI-related stock rallies in the US and in markets such as Taiwan and South Korea, PTI reported. Lower crude oil prices and a weak dollar also supported the currency.

The flow numbers show the scale of the reversal. Foreign investors pumped in Rs 84,290 crore into Indian equities over nine trading sessions between November 2 and 13, according to depository data cited by PTI — a strong comeback after net withdrawals of Rs 34,843 crore in October and Rs 35,861 crore in September. With the latest inflows, cumulative foreign portfolio outflows from Indian equities in 2026 have narrowed to around Rs 2.1 lakh crore, from nearly Rs 3 lakh crore a few weeks ago. Foreign institutional investors bought equities worth a further Rs 7,411.41 crore on Thursday, according to exchange data.

"We expect the rupee to trade with a positive bias on strength in the domestic markets and sustained foreign inflows. Falling crude oil prices and other commodities also supported the rupee as it may ease import bills."

— Anuj Choudhary, Research Analyst, Mirae Asset Sharekhan, quoted by PTI

Stocks and oil moved the same way

Domestic equities extended their run. The Sensex surged 897.96 points, or 1.08 per cent, to settle at 83,919.71, while the Nifty climbed 286.30 points, or 1.12 per cent, to 25,800.60; both indices had ended the preceding session with gains of more than 1 per cent, PTI reported. Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, was trading 1.82 per cent lower at $90.31 per barrel in futures trade, and the dollar index, which gauges the greenback against a basket of six currencies, was at 103.87, lower by 0.08 per cent.

What it means if you send money to India

The rally cuts both ways for the diaspora. Anyone remitting dollars to India this week receives fewer rupees per dollar than at any point since April: $1,000 converts to about Rs 92,670 at Friday's provisional close, before fees and provider margins, against about Rs 94,190 at the November 13 close of 94.19. The same strength, if it holds, works in India's favour on the import side, since a stronger rupee lowers the rupee cost of crude and other imports.

What to watch next

Choudhary said traders may take cues from revised consumer sentiment data from the US, and expected the USD-INR spot price to trade in a range of Rs 92.40 to Rs 93. Whether the rupee holds above the 93 level will depend on the foreign inflows continuing; the September and October outflow figures in the same PTI report are a reminder of how quickly those flows have reversed this year.

key_takeaways: Rupee closes at 92.67 against the dollar, above 93 for the first time in seven months.
Foreign investors injected Rs 84,290 crore into Indian equities from November 2 to 13.
Rupee appreciated over 1.6% since November 13, when it closed at 94.19.
Domestic equities surged, with Sensex gaining 897.96 points to settle at 83,919.71.
Lower crude oil prices and a weak dollar supported the rupee's strength.
